question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to spec with the narrowed Round A scope.

Why: your question is now answerable from the app, and this re-scope drops an 18-year archive project you do not need in order to answer it. It also refuses to give you a comparison before making the comparison honest, which is the part that would otherwise waste your time.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 060 to spec, where an agent writes the specification for Round A — 2023 versus 2025 from production data, payer-controlled, with 2024 as a partial-year shape check. Reject holds it at ideation.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE, ONE THING YOU CAN TEST IN TWO MINUTES that may dissolve the question:

Your 2025 records two people; 2023 and 2024 record one. 2025 splits wei 952 rows / ijac 452. All 1,670 rows of 2023-2024 carry ijac, and that is your own ruling from 061 D2a — the Daily tab has no payer column because it only ever had one payer. There is no wei record for those years.

Open Reports, Annual, 2025, and filter to ijac. Compare that against unfiltered 2023. If that single control closes most of the gap, the answer to "why did it double" is "you started recording a second person", and the alarming premise behind this whole entity dissolves. Worth doing before you approve, because it may change what you want spec to do.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO PREMISES YOU HAVE BEEN CARRYING:

(1) 2024 is not a full year — it stops on 2024-11-08, short by 53 days. Its annual total understates a real year, so it cannot be compared naively against a complete 2023 or 2025. It is a shape check, not a total.

(2) NT$1.2M/year is not what the app measures, for any year. That figure is total annual living cost. The app holds no rent, no mortgage, no insurance and no utilities in either era, and the 2023-2024 rows are only the workbook's variable-expense tab. Comparing app totals against NT$1.2M compares two different things, and doing so would have produced a confident wrong answer.

ONE THING THAT IS BLOCKED AND NEEDS YOU EVENTUALLY, NOT NOW: extending before 2023. The eighteen archive files for 2006-2021 are read by no working credential — the Drive connector is bound to a work account, the staging service account was granted one file, the production one gets 403. That is a sharing or rebinding action only you can take, and Round B would need it.

artifacts.summary:
SEED OUTCOME, sharpened by the captain: answer why her recorded spending roughly doubled between 2023-2024 and 2025, then propose a realistic path back down. The original framing was an analysis report over every archive year since 2006; her actual question is a three-year comparison that the app can now serve.

WHY THE SCOPE COLLAPSED, in a good way: entity 061 imported 2023 and 2024 into production, so three consecutive years of daily records now sit in one schema, in the app's own category taxonomy. 2023: 895 rows, all twelve months. 2024: 775 rows, ending 2024-11-08. 2025: 1,404 rows, twelve months, from the 008 CSV migration. Reports > Annual already produces, per year, the annual total, per-category breakdown with count and share, per-payer breakdown, twelve-bar monthly trend and an AI insight. The year arrows are unbounded, so all three years are reachable today. So the WHAT of her question is three screens; this entity's remaining job is the WHY and the path back, which no screen produces.

INCLUDED SCOPE — Round A: 2023 versus 2025 from production data only, payer-controlled before any explanation is offered, with 2024 as a partial-year shape corroboration. Deliverable: the honest comparison, the labelled reasons, and a first glide path expressed against what the app actually measures.

EXCLUDED SCOPE — deferred to a possible Round B: what the sub-NT$1.2M years actually counted, which requires the workbook's non-Daily tabs (the annual matrix over 25 buckets including five income-side, the category-by-month rollup, and the multi-decade projection carrying her own per-year required-spending column to 2041); anything before 2023, which is credential-blocked; and 2022, which belongs to entity 062.

THE PROOF NEEDED TO DECIDE WHETHER SPECCING SHOULD START — three traps that must be controlled or the comparison means the wrong thing, every one of which makes 2025 look larger for reasons that are not spending:

1. PAYER ASYMMETRY. 2025 counts two people, 2023-2024 count one. Controllable in the app right now with the Reports payer filter, which resolves through resolvePayerName and filters on the stored display name. This must be established FIRST because every other explanation is conditional on it.

2. 2024's TRUNCATION. Record ends 2024-11-08; the workbook's own December month total and day sum are both zero, so the fortnight was never entered and nothing recovers it. Short by 53 days. Usable as shape, not as an annual total, unless explicitly annualized and labelled.

3. TAXONOMY AND COVERAGE DRIFT. The 2023-2024 rows are the workbook's variable-expense tab only — no income rows, no fixed-expense rows. The 2025 CSV's nine buckets are a different scheme from the workbook's nine, and each migration mapped its own scheme into the app's categories independently. Two visible consequences: 2025 carries a recurring-digital-subscriptions bucket with no counterpart in 2023-2024, and 2025's fitness spending sits in a health bucket where 2023-2024 mapped only a handful of rows to Sports. Each is EITHER a real behaviour change OR a recording-coverage change, and the app cannot distinguish them.

ALSO RECORDED: four October 2023 rows exist in her workbook only as a month figure and are therefore absent from the app — 061 Finding 6 names them. If a category comparison lands on any of them, part of the difference is there.

DELIVERY CONSTRAINT, unchanged and restated with its reason: this repository is public and the report is nothing but real figures, so the report is delivered privately and the entity records only its location. No money figure appears in the entity, a commit message, or any repo file. Verified on this cycle: the only 6-plus-digit numbers in the entity are SHA-256 digest fragments and a spreadsheet gid.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING: 4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed.

WHY SPLIT RATHER THAN RUN BOTH: Round A is nearly free and Round B is not. If the payer control explains most of the gap, the alarming premise behind this entity dissolves and Round B becomes calm rather than urgent. Running them together spends the expensive half before knowing whether it is needed.
